To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Early Palaeo-zoic high-grade metamorphic event in the Andes of NW Argentina/N Chile is characterized by mid- to deep crustal metamorphism, with peak temperatures commonly above 650°C, at pressures of ~0.5–1.0 Gpa; the metamorphism occurred at 500 and 430 Ma; it is associated with the formation of felsic magmatic rocks, and with the recycling of old crust, without significant addition of new crust.

the Early Palaezoic crust in the Central Andes is characterized by a complex tectonic history of reworking and recycling of pre-Palaeo-zoic crust, and that this crustal material was reworked during the Cambrian–Ordovician orogenic events at the active margin of West Gondo-wana.

(i) the Early Palaeoic high-grade metamorphic belt in the Andes of NW Argentina and NChile is characterized by midcrust temperatures commonly above the solidus, (ii) it is characterized by pressures between 0.5 and 0.7 GPA, locally up to 1.0GPA, and (iii) the metamorphism took place at 530-500 Ma and 470-420Ma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(1) high-grade metamorphic conditions and age of the basement in the Andes of NW Argentina and N. Chile; (2) the composition of the Early Palæozoic
the evolution of a continental margin of Gondwana during Early Palaeozoics times, which was dominated by the accretion of pre-existing Gondwanan crust.
the evolution of a continental arc and subsequent orogenic cycle of the Early Palæozoic Andean basement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Early Palaeo-zoic orogenic evolution of the Andes is dominated by reworking and recycling of pre-existing continental crust.

the Early Palaeo-zoic high-grade metamorphic belt in the Andes between 18° and 31° S was a continental margin orogen with a mid-crust temperature regime, and that the crustal residence ages indicate that it formed from re-cycled crust without major contributions from accretion of exotic material.

the high-grade metamorphism of the Early Palaozoic basement in the Andes is the result of an active margin setting, with the formation of felsic crust by crustal melting, and that the Early Palaeozic basement is a composite of reworked pre-Palaeozic crust, with a dominant component of ca. 2 Ga age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Early Palaeo-zoic crust of the Andes was formed by recycling of pre-Palaeo-zoicoic crust.
the Early Palaeoic orogen of the Andes was an intracontinental collisional belt.
the Early Palaeoic orogen of the Andes is a reworking of the pre-Palaeoic crust of the West Gondwane supercontinent, which is consistent with the absence of exotic material in the isotope signatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the orogen is a composite of reworked crustal material.
the high-grade metamorphism is a product of the collision between West Gondwanda and the proto-Pacific plate.
the orogenic cycle in the Andes between 18° and 33° S is a single event with two distinct pulses of metamorphism, which are separated by ~50 Ma.
